text:
nina: hi all! day 2, trying to standardize my dotfiles. i've switched to fish shell and installed asdf. asdf seems to work in terminal but direnv and 1password CLI helpers aren't picked up inside fish. also gpg signing for git fails with 'no pinentry'. any quick fish + mac tips?

samir: welcome nina :wave: fish is great but it's not POSIX, so most asdf instructions are for bash/zsh. for fish you should add the asdf fish integration lines and prepare PATH. check `~/.config/fish/config.fish` for: 
```
set -x PATH $HOME/.asdf/shims $PATH
source $HOME/.asdf/asdf.fish
```
that usually gets shims in front.

emily: for direnv you need the fish hook: `direnv hook fish` in your config.fish. example: `eval (direnv hook fish)` — put that after asdf lines so direnv can see the shims.

nina: ok added those. 1password CLI problem is weird: when i run `op signin` in terminal it works and injects `OP_SESSION_xxx` env var, but VS Code terminal doesn't see it and some git hooks run without the env. i used the mac 1Password app integration to enable SSH agent, but CLI session is per-shell. any way to persist?

samir: OP sessions are ephemeral by design. we recommend using the 1Password desktop app's SSH agent for keys and then enabling the CLI auto-signin with a permanent session via `op account sign-in --session`. Alternatively, store a short script in `~/.config/fish/functions/op-restore.fish` that re-establishes session from 1Password's secure item, but that's advanced. simpler: launch apps from a terminal where you ran `eval $(op signin ...)` or add `eval (op signin --sh)` to your fish config if you accept interactive signin at login.

emily: caution about putting `op signin` in config.fish if it requires a password or MFA prompt at each session. another option is to run a login shell once and export the session to `~/.op_session` then source it in config.fish if your org allows that.

nina: noted. last bit: gpg/pinentry. when i run `git commit -S` it fails with pinentry error. i installed gpg with brew and `pinentry-mac`, and set `gpgconf --launch gpg-agent`, but fish still complains.

samir: for mac + pinentry-mac you need to tell gpg-agent which pinentry to use. add to `~/.gnupg/gpg-agent.conf`: `pinentry-program /opt/homebrew/bin/pinentry-mac` and then `gpgconf --kill gpg-agent` to reload. also ensure `GPG_TTY` is set, but on mac GUI it isn't necessary; for terminal add `set -x GPG_TTY (tty)` to config.fish.

emily: and if VS Code's git uses a different shell env, make sure you open code from a terminal (`code .`) so it inherits the same GPG_AGENT_INFO / session. otherwise you can configure `git` to use `gpg` through `gpg2` explicit path in `~/.gitconfig`: 
```
[gpg]
    program = /opt/homebrew/bin/gpg
```

nina: ok after updating gpg-agent.conf and restarting agent `git commit -S` now succeeds in terminal. i still need to figure the 1Password CLI persistence for GUI apps.

emily: one more tip: fish has `abbr` for quick dotfile snippets, we add `abbr -a asdfn 'source $HOME/.asdf/asdf.fish; and asdf reshim'` for new hires. feel free to PR your dotfile snippet to https://redwood.internal/dotfiles and tag @devx for review.

devx-bot: Welcome @nina! Thanks for documenting these steps. If you open a short PR with your fish snippets and the `gpg-agent.conf` note, we'll include it in the onboarding guide. :robot_face:
